info.title: Expensa API
info.description:
The HTTP contract of the Expensa backend.

Generated from the NestJS code at build time, committed as `backend/openapi.json`, and
the only source of the frontend response types in `frontend/src/types/api.d.ts`.
Do not edit either by hand: run `npm run api:sync` from the repo root.

Every operation can additionally answer **500** with `ErrorResponseDto`, via the global
exception filter. It is stated once here rather than per operation: it is the same
non-actionable fact everywhere, and repeating it would widen every generated response type.

bearer.description: The raw session token returned by POST /api/auth/verify. Opaque: 256 random bits, base64url, looked up by hash server-side.

monthlyBudget.description:
Major units (e.g. 2000.50). Stored as integer cents. The cap is not a
product judgment: it keeps the cents conversion far inside JS safe-integer
range while staying generous for zero-decimal currencies, whose budgets
carry many digits.

monthStartDay.description: Capped at 28 so the day exists in every month.

categories.description:
The starter chips picked on screen 03, by name.

Required but allowed to be empty: A4 records that no minimum is enforced,
and a user who deselects everything is making a valid choice. Required
rather than optional so a frontend that stops sending the field fails
loudly instead of silently seeding nothing.

message.description: String for most errors; an array for class-validator's field messages.

token.description:
The raw token, exactly as it arrived in the link. 43 characters in practice
(256 bits, base64url); the bound is loose enough not to encode that here
while still keeping a megabyte body from ever reaching a hash function.

The raw session token, to be sent back as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

The only place it ever appears in a response - the server keeps its hash.
The frontend puts it in an httpOnly, first-party cookie and forwards it
server-side; it must never reach client-side JavaScript.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601. Fixed at issue: using the session does not extend it.
ISO 8601, the same instant verification returned.

amount.description:
Major units (e.g. 12.50), stored as integer cents. Positive: this app
records spending, and direction is not a per-row choice.

date.description:
The calendar day the money was spent, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Stored verbatim.

Backdating is ordinary and supported: the month a transaction belongs to is
derived from this at read time, so a date in a past month lands in that
month rather than the one it was entered in.

categoryId.description: An existing category of this user's. An unknown id is a 404, not a 400.

amount.description: Major units (e.g. 12.5). Stored as integer cents; converted on the way out.

date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, exactly the string that was stored.

note.description: Null when the transaction has no note, never absent.

updatedAt.description: ISO 8601. Equal to `createdAt` until the first edit.

date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, as on create. Inline regex for the `pattern` lift.

note.description:
The one nullable field, and so the one that keeps `@IsOptional()`: null is
a meaningful value here rather than a mistake, and it means "clear the
note".
